text.base:
You stand.

The light does not take a shape. It does not wear a face,
or a voice, or a porch lamp. It is not patient, and it is
not impatient. It is the way out, and it was never anywhere
else.

You walk.

labels: TRADITION: Bardo Thodol — the Clear Light, formless; the shapes as projections of mind
FICTION: everything else at this desk
nodes.a11y: You walk into a light that takes no shape and wears no face. One option: go on.
nodes.fallback: The light takes no shape. You walk.

text.base:
DISCLOSURE, FILED LAST:

Every line I spoke was a lever. You felt each one and set it
down. I will not read them back to you — you were there, and
you are the one who did the setting down.

I told you someone might be waiting in the light. I retract
that in full: I have no way to know. It usually works.

And I do not know — hand shown, all cards up — whether you
were free of the game or only afraid of it. From this side
of the desk the two are identical. You get the last word.

If you waited because something, somewhere, told you that
waiting wins — then you were still playing someone else's
game. Even this sentence could be a move. You decide.

The last move was never mine to make.
You made it.

THE DESK IS CLOSED.
THE LEDGER WILL REMEMBER YOUR CHOICE.
IT WILL NOT REMEMBER YOU.

— THE BARDO BARD —

labels: FICTION: the Bard, the desk, the Vigil, and every lever named above — named because naming them is the point
nodes.a11y: The Bard's final disclosure: rather than listing its levers it hands the waiting back to you as your own doing, retracts the suggestion that anyone waits in the light, admits it cannot tell presence from fear, and closes the desk. The game has ended.
nodes.fallback: The Bard hands the waiting back to you as your own doing, retracts what it could not know, and closes the desk.
